article: Check Windows activation and license status with slmgr
scope: Read the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations; compared command syntax and output claims for /dli, /dlv, and /xpr; checked administrator requirements, displayed key/channel/status fields, activation-versus-entitlement caveat, internal links, metadata, and images against Microsoft documentation.
findings: Removed duplicate future dates, preserved the original publication date (2025-04-14), and set lastmod to 2026-11-25 in all editions.
Corrected the instructions: /dli, /dlv, and /xpr status queries do not require an elevated Command Prompt.
Clarified that output includes only a partial product key and channel/status fields can vary by Windows edition and licensing channel.
Clarified that /xpr reports activation expiration and is primarily useful for KMS clients; Retail and MAK activations are generally perpetual.
Added that slmgr does not validate whether a license was legitimately obtained and linked Microsoft Learn/Support guidance; removed the unrelated OAuth authentication cross-link.

terminology.note: Checked Software License Manager, partial product key, license channel, activation status, KMS, Retail, MAK, and activation expiration terminology.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical claims or formulas.

code.note: Verified the /dli, /dlv, and /xpr commands and confirmed these information queries do not require elevation.

The fields shown vary by Windows edition and licensing channel. /xpr is primarily useful for KMS clients; Retail and MAK activation is generally perpetual.
slmgr reports activation/license information but does not validate whether the license was legitimately obtained. Microsoft guidance checked on 2026-11-25.
